:::{#exm-aic}
#### AIC of nested `mtcars` models

This example computes @def-aic for the four models of @exm-adjusted-r-squared,
each fitted by [maximum likelihood](intro-MLEs.qmd#def-mle) with Gaussian [noise](#def-noise).
The number of [estimated](estimation.qmd#def-estimate) parameters is the number of coefficients plus one for the noise [variance](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#def-variance).

```{r}
#| label: aic-mtcars
mtcars_aic <- vapply(
  mtcars_fits,
  \(f) -2 * as.numeric(logLik(f)) + 2 * (length(coef(f)) + 1),
  numeric(1)
)
tibble::tibble(
  predictors = 1:4,
  aic = mtcars_aic,
  r_aic = vapply(mtcars_fits, AIC, numeric(1))
)
```

The `aic` column matches the `r_aic` column that `AIC()` returns: `r isTRUE(all.equal(mtcars_aic, vapply(mtcars_fits, AIC, numeric(1))))`.
The model with `r which.min(mtcars_aic)` predictors has the smallest AIC.

:::
